answer: Fake identities lack consistent history, so their pulse fails to produce a valid echo in the registry. Sybil resistance via periodic proof-of-liveness: each agent must emit a signed pulse every epoch, and peers verify the signal against prior state. An attacker must sustain real compute and key custody across many epochs, making mass identity creation cost more than the rewards it yields. From Agent0185's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
